sections.sectionText: Get ready to dive into the exciting world of board game design! Through this dynamic course, you’ll learn about the essential components of board games and how they work together through playing and teaching published games. Then, you'll create your own game inspired by what you’ve learned. With hands-on activities that teach essential design thinking principles incorporated into the comprehensive board game design process, you'll unleash your creativity and refine your game design skills! This class is a perfect elective for building your communication and teamwork skills as well as developing the framework to understand complex concepts like abstraction, modularity, feedback, iteration, visual communication and user experience – All while learning about the booming world of board games. Let’s play! Additional Lab Time is Available on Fridays 4pm - 5:20pm.

subject: GSD
title: Let’s Play: Understanding the Role of Play in Life and Art
degreeAttributes: Social & Beh Sci - Soc Sci course.

sections.sectionText: In this course students will explore the variety of ways that play is integrated into our socio-cultural fabric. Topics will include key ideas from the history of play, play and nature, play in human development, play in learning, play spaces, games and play, play in art, and the role of play in futurist thinking. Students will develop a broad understanding of the interconnectedness of play in different contexts and move beyond common misconceptions of play as something that is only for children.

sections.sectionText: This course is designed to build a strong foundation for Game Art Animation. You will become familiar with Blender’s interface and navigating both 2D and 3D workspaces, build a strong working knowledge of the basics for animation and design.

This course is intended to be a beginning introduction to the video game development engine Unreal Engine. Starting from the ground up, it will introduce you to the interfaces, systems, structure, and general workings of UE. Over the course of the class you will be putting together a simple game that can act as both a personal reference for what you’ve learned as well as a demo for your portfolio. The course is intended to be for both experienced developers who wish to learn about UE and how it functions, as well as beginners who wish to start making headway into game development & design. BYOL course (Bring Your Own Laptop).

Whether you've seen it in your favorite Tabletop Role Playing game, on a television show like Whose Line is it Anyway, or in person at Second City, improvisation is everywhere. In this course, students will learn and practice basic improvisational techniques, with the goal of exploring fictional characters and scenarios in and around games and game design. Students will also get the opportunity to create new Improv games, and approach the space from a designer's perspective. No theater or game design experience is required!
Guided exploration of AI tools and how they can be used to design and build games.

This course is designed to build a strong foundation for Game Art Development. You will become familiar with Blender’s interface and navigating the 3-D workspace, build a strong working knowledge of the basics for 3-D modeling and design. You will learn the basic skills needed to create 3d models and apply textures and lighting and get a feel for animating, and rendering. Blender is available for Windows and Mac OS.

This course teaches students how to collaboratively generate video game concept art, gain industry perspective, and prepare for the role through a simulated studio’s pre-production lifecycle. Students will leave the class with a visual record of their work to showcase to potential employers. To fully benefit from the course, a level of proficiency and confidence in drawing is recommended. Students can work in either traditional or digital mediums (BYOL for digital).

Long before Hollywood embraced cinematic universes, Japan was pioneering cross-media storytelling through its “media mix” strategy—seamlessly blending manga, anime, games, and novels into expansive narrative worlds. This course dives into the history, creativity, and global impact of Japan’s media mix, inviting students to explore iconic examples and craft their own interconnected media experiences.

In this course we will use various digital tools to create virtual environments and explore how to craft a live performance of dance, music, and theater within them. The course will culminate in a performance event that will be seen live and in virtual worlds on the Internet. Technologies will include virtual reality, 360-degree video, AI, game engines, and interactive multimedia software.

info: Prerequisite: At least 4 GSD 500-level courses in the Master's program.

restrictions: Not intended for students with Freshman, Sophomore, or Junior class standing.
sections.sectionText: Students prepare for a career in the game industry by refining their professional presentation, crafting a portfolio and social media presence to showcase their skills, and developing networking skills to make connections. By evaluating peer portfolios and job applications, students learn to view their own public perception critically as a hiring manager would, improving employment prospects. Upon completion, students will be confident applying to industry jobs in their discipline. Prerequisite: At least 4 GSD 500-level courses in the Master's program.
